lead: Runtime defense, code approval and cross-request safety monitoring expose distinct enforcement and data-custody questions. A dated places benchmark makes grading limits visible; product rollouts, investment automation and legal reporting keep claims separate from verified outcomes.

The late-morning batch tests the boundary between verifiable code properties and general correctness. A UK agent rollout, provider-data incidents and competing accounts of AI economics retain source-specific limits; an inaccessible interview is not reconstructed.

The afternoon batch separates a major algebraic-complexity claim from verified quantum resource reductions. Customer interviews, messy-workplace benchmarks and internal safety reporting probe different limits of agent deployment; market reactions and corporate transactions retain their dated, source-specific scope.

sections.title: Runtime shields and static scanners protect different boundaries
sections.intro: A temporary Linux mitigation and a configuration scanner describe scoped defenses, not universal protection.

sections.title: Approval policies and zero retention describe different contracts
sections.intro: Claude Ship separates repair from approval; EFS moves storage custody without eliminating monitoring or costs.

sections.title: Local facts need dated keys and repeatable judgments
sections.intro: PlaceBench exposes its grading and repeat limits, while a chart alpha distinguishes suggestions from full-query aggregation.

sections.title: Unified workspaces are not permission to connect accounts
sections.intro: A demo inbox and a multi-pane IDE describe capabilities rather than tested privacy guarantees.

sections.title: Product rollouts and portfolios keep claims separate from outcomes
sections.intro: A reported model rollout, a satellite first close and an investing beta do not establish universal availability or performance.

sections.title: Prosecutors make allegations, not findings of guilt
sections.intro: Two reports about a former OpenAI engineer retain their separate access limits and distinguish a prosecution filing from adjudicated facts.

sections.title: Career anxiety is not a labor-market forecast
sections.intro: An Ask HN thread brings conflicting personal views, not a representative estimate of which jobs automation will change.

sections.title: Compiler checks and source maps do not prove an application correct
sections.intro: Declare and Genesis expose specific checks and small experiments, with clear limits on what those checks cover.

sections.title: Token growth and shared loss curves leave different economic questions open
sections.intro: An economic essay separates price from volume, while a roundup keeps development-limit proposals and unofficial forecasts distinct.

sections.title: Agent rollout and data policy require more than product assurances
sections.intro: Muse coverage preserves consumer-risk warnings; OpenRouter coverage distinguishes confirmed accounts from precautionary eligibility changes.

sections.title: Runtime defense retains an operator and a permanent-patch requirement
sections.intro: Secondary Shirudo coverage is read against the narrower primary demonstration and deployment controls.

sections.title: A cancer timeline is not a clinical result
sections.intro: A pharma executive's reported skepticism keeps its missing interview context and does not settle the value of particular AI-assisted treatments.

sections.title: Mathematical claims need distinct models and independent checks
sections.intro: A new algebraic-circuit preprint is a claim to examine, while a researcher profile does not replace the narrower Riemann verification record.

sections.title: Verified quantum circuits are not yet practical scientific runs
sections.intro: DeepMind reports resource improvements to selected algorithms and retains the hardware gap.

sections.title: Weight editing, RL infrastructure and residual routing change different layers
sections.intro: SelfWrite studies bounded edits, Rocket describes long training runs and DCA revisits earlier architecture research.

sections.title: Workplace gains coexist with bottlenecks and incomplete agent tasks
sections.intro: A customer-interview study and a workplace benchmark measure different sides of deployment, with distinct sample limits.

sections.title: Internal safety debates do not establish an industry-wide pause
sections.intro: Axios reports concern and company responses; Marcus adds an explicitly prescriptive argument.

sections.title: Market snapshots are not forecasts or closing prices
sections.intro: Intraday reporting and commentary retain their timestamps, access limits and separation from technical performance.

sections.title: Compute deals and data-workload funding retain their transaction scope
sections.intro: Decart technology and talent are the reported acquisition target; Zipher savings remain sourced claims.

sections.title: Export controls and lab security need their missing primary context
sections.intro: A Bloomberg opening and an inaccessible FT report support only bounded descriptions.

sections.title: Agent control and individual power remain contested arguments
sections.intro: Harley, Doctorow and Thompson offer different accounts of provider control, market barriers and exceptional individuals.

sections.title: Parallel coding still leaves a human attention bottleneck
sections.intro: A creator account describes status management rather than measured autonomous throughput.

sections.title: Voice payments separate a demo from compliance evidence
sections.intro: Natural describes a dedicated payment call, while Grok local computer controls remain unreleased development settings.

sections.title: Small-business assistance has a defined pilot audience
sections.intro: OpenWorks lists communities, eligibility and partner support rather than universal access.
